sources.title: The Semantic Content of the General Classifier in Mandarin
sources.summary_en: The authors review competing analyses of Mandarin ge and argue, on corpus and experimental grounds, that it functions as a grammatical default without an inherent core meaning. They give yi-ge ren as ‘a person’ among examples of individual classifiers. This supports the construction and shows why it would overstate the evidence to assign 个 a fixed lexical meaning such as ‘individual.’

sources.title: 论量词“个”的语源—兼谈“个”“介”之别
sources.summary_en: The accessible abstract reports the author's challenge to the account that 个 derives from 介 ‘separate/individual,’ and proposes instead that 个 originally meant an arrow used as a counting token, later developing into a general classifier. This is the author's proposed historical account, not proof of the modern classifier's derivation.

sources.title: 一個 — 维基词典
sources.summary_en: The Chinese entry analyzes 一個 as numeral 一 plus general classifier 個/个, while also listing distinct uses such as ‘whole’ and ‘same.’ It is a community-edited reference; the target construction is independently supported by the Ministry dictionary and linguistic sources.

claims.text_en: In the supplied example, 一个 modifies 大汉 and denotes one person. 一 supplies the cardinal value ‘one’; 个 is the classifier in the numeral-classifier construction, which presents the person as one counted unit. The example does not specify the person’s identity or any narrower subtype.

The relevant sense is the dictionary’s quantity sense (‘a single item’), not its separate senses for an entire span or for degree before a predicate. The dictionary’s example 一個少年將軍 and the linguistic example yi-ge ren support use with a person.

The classifier’s contribution should be described cautiously: linguistic sources support its role in marking a unit of quantification, while one specialist study argues that general ge is a grammatical default without an inherent core meaning. The evidence does not justify glossing 个 itself as carrying a fixed meaning ‘individual.’

A 2024 article abstract challenges the account that classifier 个 derives from 介 ‘separate/individual’ and proposes an arrow-to-counting-token-to-general-classifier path. This is an author's proposal; the accessible abstract does not establish that history as fact or prove the derivation of modern 一个.

sources.summary_en: This linguistic study distinguishes duration-reference 一会（儿） from a later time-position use. It analyzes 一会（儿） after a verb as measuring the action's duration and argues that the duration expression developed from 一 + 会, initially interpreted as ‘one gathering.’ The study proposes that comparison with separation helped yield a short-time meaning, which lexicalized by the Song period; it then traces a distinct time-position use through grammaticalization. The study's proposed historical analysis takes 一会 back to the phrase 一 + 会, ‘one gathering,’ and suggests that contrast with separation could make the interval seem short. It reports that the short-duration use became lexicalized by the Song period. This is an argued historical pathway, not evidence that the parts retain those meanings in modern 一会儿.

The study distinguishes duration 一会（儿） from a time-position use that can mean ‘after a short while’ in suitable contexts, and proposes that the latter developed through grammaticalization from duration use in adverbial contexts. The supplied postverbal example is the duration use, not that separate time-position use.
儿 here is an erhua suffix: the Ministry of Education dictionary describes this suffix as generally without its own meaning. It does not add a separately supported duration or quantity meaning to 一会儿.

sources.title: Approximate numbers – ChinGram
sources.summary_en: This specialist grammar reference says 多 after a number containing units such as 十, 百, or 千 marks a broader approximate range. It gives 一百多米 as more than 100 and approximately 100–200, and 两百多个小时 as more than 200 and approximately 200–300 hours. It does not discuss 三百多个乡勇 specifically.

claims.text_en: For the supplied cardinal-number sense, 三 contributes three and 百 contributes one hundred, yielding three hundred (3 × 100). The dictionaries' separate nonnumerical senses for the characters do not fit this use.

In the example 三百多个乡勇, 三百 supplies the base quantity 300. 多 after this round number indicates an approximate quantity above 300; 个 is the classifier before the noun. The example context applies that quantity to 乡勇, but the supplied word 三百 itself means three hundred.

ChinGram's examples place 一百多 in an approximate 100–200 range and 两百多个 in an approximate 200–300 range. Extending that stated pattern to 三百多个 suggests a broad approximate range above 300 and below 400. This is an inference from the general pattern, not a source's analysis of the supplied phrase.

sources.title: 三国演义·第一回 宴桃园豪杰三结义　斩黄巾英雄首立功｜古文岛
sources.summary_en: The passage first describes Guan Yu's troops hiding on the left and Zhang Fei's on the right, then Liu Bei's force turning back to attack; it calls the resulting attack 三路夹攻. This context supports three coordinated attacking contingents or approaches, without naming exact compass directions.

sources.title: 〈左右夾攻〉辭典檢視｜教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》2021
sources.summary_en: Defines 左右夾攻 as a tactic of attacking in a pincer formation from the left and right. This clarifies 夾攻, but the headword is 左右夾攻, not 三路夾攻.

claims.text_en: In this military use, 三 contributes the count three and 路 contributes routes or lines of movement. The Ministry of Education dictionary explicitly gives 兵分三路 as an example under 路線, and the 封神演義 passage uses 三路分兵 for troops assigned to separate routes toward passes.

In the supplied 三路夾攻 context, 三路 refers to three coordinated attacking contingents or approaches: the narrative identifies forces on the left and right and Liu Bei's force turning back to attack. The word 路 by itself denotes routes or lines, so translating the phrase contextually as “three attacking forces” is supported by the passage, rather than by 三路 as a fixed standalone meaning. The exact compass directions are not specified.

夾攻 contributes the attack-from-the-sides or pincer-attack notion. The cited dictionary describes this as attack from the left and right; in the supplied passage that meaning combines with the three contingents to describe their coordinated assault. It does not establish a precise formation beyond what the narrative states.

sources.title: 方向補語（動詞）「下来」 | 中国語文法辞典
sources.summary_en: A grammar reference that lists a persistence use of verb + 下来, describing continuation from past to present or over an interval from beginning to end. Its examples are 保存下来 and 坚持下来, not 活下来. It also describes the spatial compound as downward movement toward the speaker and says 来 has a complement-like role in the compound.

sources.title: 方向補語「下来」は上から下への移動を表す – 中国語初級から中級者向けのメルマガバックナンバー
sources.summary_en: A Chinese-learning reference that directly gives 我到现在拼命地活下来了 and explains that this example describes an action continuing up to the present. This supports a temporal-persistence reading of 活下来, though it does not establish a precise semantic contribution for 下 and 来 separately in that extended use.

sources.title: 〖中国語文法基礎〗方向補語の派生義｜「上」「出」「起」「下来」等
sources.summary_en: A grammar guide, drawing on a named modern Chinese grammar reference, distinguishes 下来’s separation/retention use from a state-change use in which a dynamic situation settles into a state. Its discussion of temporal continuation focuses on 下去, so it does not independently support treating all 下来 examples as the same persistence sense.

sources.title: 汉语趋向补语“下来”“下去”的空间、时间、状态义及其对外汉语教学
sources.summary_en: An opened 2019 thesis by Sun Yuchen, hosted on Scribd. It describes the common teaching distinction of 下来 as continuation from past to present and 下去 as continuation from present to future, but cautions that this division is not absolute. It reports corpus examples of 下来 with future-oriented continuations and cites Sugimura (1983) for a more nuanced account involving a retrospective temporal viewpoint. It is a thesis, not a primary historical study.

claims.text_en: The supplied sense is a reasonable construction-level description of temporal persistence: the reference’s 下来 examples 保存下来 and 坚持下来 are described as continuing from the past to the present or across an interval, and another opened guide directly uses 活下来 in 我到现在拼命地活下来了. These sources support persistence through a time span, but they do not show that every 下来 occurrence has this meaning.

In the supplied sentence, whether Dong Zhuo can 活下来 can be rendered generally as whether he can survive or remain alive. The sentence does not identify a particular threat, means of survival, or exact time interval, so those details should not be added to the gloss.

The source describes spatial 下来 as downward movement toward the speaker, and treats 来 as complement-like within the compound. That spatial description does not establish a distinct literal contribution of 来 in the extended persistence use 活下来; the supported explanation is for 下来 as a whole constructional complement.

The usual past-to-present description is a useful pattern, not a fully reliable boundary: the opened thesis reports future-oriented 下来 examples and discusses an analysis in which the temporal use can look back from a reference point while an action or state continues. This cautions against assigning a fixed endpoint such as the moment of speaking to the supplied example.

The sources support a relationship between spatial directional complements and extended meanings, but the material opened here does not establish a specific historical derivation of the persistence reading in 活下来. The modern examples and general statements about grammaticalization do not by themselves prove that derivation.

sources.title: 汉典：不满
sources.summary_en: The word explanation distinguishes ‘not reaching saturation,’ ‘feeling something lacking or displeasure,’ and ‘not being worth [a value].’ Its separate 国语辞典 section lists ‘insufficient/not enough’ and ‘not satisfied’; the emotional sense is cited from Tang writer Han Yu.

sources.title: 汉典：满意
sources.summary_en: Defines 满意 as having one’s wishes fulfilled or being in accord with one’s wishes. Its 国语辞典 section gives ‘符合心意’ (‘accord with one’s wishes’) and separately records the older/different use 满以为 (‘expect, suppose’).

claims.text_en: For the target emotional sense, dictionaries gloss 不满 as 不满意 (‘not satisfied’). This supports a present-day explanation in which 不 negates the satisfied state expressed by 满意; 汉典 explains 满意 as wishes being fulfilled or accord with one’s wishes. The word itself does not specify what the person is dissatisfied with.

The emotional sense is distinct from the separately listed quantity sense ‘insufficient/not enough.’ The supplied example uses the emotional sense; it does not establish a specific object or cause for the dissatisfaction.

The dictionaries provide historical attestations of the emotional sense: 汉典 cites a Tang passage by Han Yu, and the Ministry of Education dictionary cites 初刻拍案惊奇. These attestations show the sense was used in older texts, but do not demonstrate that it developed historically from the quantity or fullness sense.

sources.title: 张荣华：“中兴”之义及“同治中兴”命名之非
sources.summary_en: The historian traces the term's earliest cited occurrence to the Mao preface to 烝民 and reports Wang Guoguo's Song-era account that 中 in 中兴 had level- and departing-tone readings: one indicated an equal midpoint, the other a position between two points whose spans need not be equal. claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 中兴 means that a declining state or dynasty recovers and flourishes. The Ministry of Education dictionary glosses the whole word as becoming vigorous and prosperous again, with 少康's restoration of Xia as its example.

The cited early occurrence is the Mao preface to 烝民, which says “任贤使能，周室中兴焉” (“appointing worthy people and employing the able, the Zhou house revived”). This supports the historical political use, but the passage does not establish a separate “again” or “revive” meaning for 中.

Zhang Ronghua reports Wang Guoguo's interpretation that 中 in 中兴 could be read with either a midpoint sense or a sense of being between two points without equal spans. Zhang also notes that this distinction does not reliably delimit historical examples. It is a reported historical analysis, not evidence that modern speakers compositionally understand 中兴 as 中 (“again”) plus 兴 (“revive”).

The article also reports an older definition of 中兴 as recovering a realm that one's own line had lost, contrasting it with 反正, where recovery was attributed to someone else. This describes a historical distinction between whole-word terms and does not by itself identify 中's independent contribution.

sources.summary_en: Taiwan’s Ministry of Education dictionary defines 亂 as ‘without order or system’ and separately as ‘unsettled, unstable,’ with examples and older citations. sources.title: 漢語多功能字庫：亂
sources.summary_en: The CUHK database interprets the bronze form 𤔔 as an early form of 亂, depicting hands working with thread or silk floss and giving ‘manage silk’ as the original sense. It proposes that unarranged thread accounts for the disordered sense, while handling the thread accounts for ‘manage/order.’ It also reports bronze uses interpreted as ‘manage’ and notes other readings or interpretations of graphic details.

sources.title: 說文解字「亂」 — Shuowen.org
sources.summary_en: The page gives the received Shuowen gloss 治也 (‘govern; put in order’) and Duan Yucai’s emendation 不治也 (‘not governed/in order’). Duan treats the positive sense as a transferred use: because what is disordered needs governing, 亂 can also mean ‘govern.’ This records Duan’s analysis rather than establishing the full historical derivation of the modern adjective.

sources.title: 楊琪：說“治” — Fudan University Center for the Study of Unearthed Texts and Paleography
sources.summary_en: Yang Qi argues that the Shuowen graph glossed 亂 as 治 (‘govern’) is an ancient form of 治, disputing Duan Yucai’s insertion of 不. The article uses transmitted and excavated graph forms to support its proposal. This is a competing specialist interpretation of the graph and positive ‘govern’ usage, not evidence that the modern adjective derives from that positive sense.

sources.title: 李春桃：說何簋銘文中的“亂”字 — Fudan University Center for the Study of Unearthed Texts and Paleography
sources.summary_en: Li Chuntao argues that a disputed inscription graph in the He gui is 亂 and means ‘govern,’ citing the Shuowen, transmitted texts, and bronze graphs. The article demonstrates continued scholarly discussion of identifying and interpreting early graphs and positive uses; it does not establish a derivation for the modern ‘disordered’ adjective.

sources.title: 亂 luàn — 汉典
sources.summary_en: Han Dian records modern and historical senses of 亂, including ‘without order/system’ and ‘unsettled/unstable,’ plus citations for both disorderly and positive governing uses. Its Shuowen and Duan Yucai sections reproduce the received gloss and Duan’s emendation. It supports the sense distinction but is not independent evidence for a semantic derivation.

claims.text_en: The supplied sense ‘disordered; chaotic’ is supported for 亂: the Ministry of Education dictionary defines it as ‘without order or system’ and separately includes ‘unsettled, unstable.’ For the example about 天下 becoming 乱, ‘chaotic’ fits the documented general disorder/social instability range; it does not require a narrower kind of disorder.

The historical sources record opposing uses or analyses: Shuowen’s received text glosses 亂 as 治 (‘govern; put in order’), while Duan Yucai emends it to 不治 (‘not in order’) and explains ‘govern’ as a transferred sense. The dictionary also records positive governing usage separately from the negative disorder sense. These contrasts should not be collapsed into a single gloss.

CUHK proposes a composition-based account in which the bronze graph depicts hands working with thread or silk floss; unarranged thread is disordered, while working it produces the ‘govern/order’ sense. This is the database’s proposed account, not independently established proof that the modern adjective developed through this precise semantic path.

A Fudan paleography article advances a competing analysis of the Shuowen graph, arguing that it is an ancient form of 治 rather than a graph meaning 不治. Another Fudan article argues for a bronze use of 亂 meaning ‘govern.’ These discussions reinforce that the early graph and positive historical use require careful distinction from the well-attested modern negative adjective; neither article demonstrates the modern adjective’s derivation.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 于是 links what follows to the preceding situation, marking it as the next event and, when the context supports it, as a result of that situation. sources.title: 于是 — 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》
sources.summary_en: The Ministry of Education dictionary defines 于是 as a conjunction marking a later event that immediately follows an earlier one. It gives a classical example and lists 於是 and 於是乎 as variants.

sources.title: 古汉语复音虚词结构模式分析 — 蓝鹰
sources.summary_en: This specialist discussion places 于 in a preposition-plus-object pattern alongside 于此 and 于何, lists 于是 in that structural class, and describes 于是 as a connective of continuation. It discusses structures of classical function words generally; it does not establish a specific modern-word derivation.

sources.title: 從“于 / 於”用法上的變化看複合詞“於是”的產生 — 楊世鐵
sources.summary_en: This historical linguistic study distinguishes prepositional phrases 于/於是 from the conjunction 于是/於是. Its author argues that the conjunction developed from 于 plus demonstrative 是 referring to a preceding situation, which could mean roughly ‘in that situation’; the phrase became more abstract and grammaticalized as a connective. The author argues against deriving the conjunction simply from the separate time-referring phrase ‘at that time,’ and notes that analyses of the forms differ.

claims.text_en: In the supplied modern sense, 于是 introduces a following event or situation in relation to what came before. The dictionary specifically supports close succession; the specialist analysis describes the conjunction as linking events with temporal succession and a logical cause-result relation. Thus “then” can fit some contexts, while “as a result” captures the relation in contexts where the preceding situation motivates or brings about what follows.

The parts have a proposed historical contribution, but they should not be assigned separate literal meanings in every modern use. In Yang’s account, 于 is a preposition and 是 is a demonstrative referring to a preceding situation, giving a source phrase roughly ‘in that situation’; increasing abstraction and grammaticalization produced the connective. This is a specialist account, not a derivation proved merely by the existence of older time or place uses of 于是.

The historical path is not presented as uncontested: Yang reports earlier analyses that derive the connective from the time-referring phrase ‘at that time,’ then argues that this phrase and the result connective are distinct and that the connective instead developed from 于 + demonstrative 是 referring to a situation. The consulted evidence supports reporting Yang’s argument, but does not settle the disagreement among analyses.

sources.title: 冯春田论著选登：疑问代词“作勿”、“是勿”的形成
sources.summary_en: Feng reviews competing accounts of 是勿. Feng favors combination of 是 and 勿 in a suitable syntactic context, and discusses how later forms including 什摩 relate to the question-word family. The article says the origins had not been settled.

A specialist historical account treats 何物 as an older interrogative meaning ‘what’ that lexicalized as a word, and proposes shortening and sound changes through forms such as 何勿, 勿/没, and 麽. This supports a historical relationship proposed for the interrogative family; it does not by itself prove every step in the derivation of present-day 什么.

The proposed later development includes 是勿/是没 and spellings such as 什摩/甚麽, with subsequent shortening. A separate study records disagreement about the earlier formation of 是勿: contraction from 是何物 has been proposed, but Feng says direct examples are lacking and favors combination of 是 with shortened interrogative 勿/物. The precise route to the modern form therefore remains a historical analysis, not a transparent modern composition.

The CUHK character entry records an older lexical meaning ‘small/fine’ for 麼 and separately says 麼 combines with 什 in modern 什麼. It does not establish that ‘small/fine’ contributes to the word’s present interrogative meaning.

sources.title: 说“以前”道“以后” (Some Remark on yiqian and yihou)

claims.text_en: The supplied ‘formerly’ sense is recorded by the dictionary as 從前, separately from 之前 (‘before’). Its examples establish both uses of 以前, including the broader past/formerly use.

In modern grammar, 以前 can follow an expression that supplies a temporal reference point, or occur without an overt preceding reference point. In either case, the word locates a time earlier than a reference point, which may be understood from context or as the utterance time.

One corpus-based thesis proposes that 以 contributes an ‘extension’ schema: from a starting point, a range extends in a direction. On this analysis, 以前 extends backward from its temporal reference point. This is a scholarly proposal about modern conceptualization, not evidence that 以 independently means ‘past’ or that this analysis is established as the sole account.

The opened dictionary and article by Niu Baoyi support the temporal meaning and reference-point grammar of the whole word, but do not independently establish a distinct present-day semantic contribution for 以. The thesis offers a specific account of that contribution; the reviewed sources do not trace it historically from older uses to modern 以前.

sources.summary_en: A Peking University journal article on the grammatical status and word-list treatment of Chinese localizers. It notes disagreement about their category and describes localizers as elements participating in word-forming combinations; it does not analyze the meaning of 以 in 以后.

sources.title: 《搜神记》介词“以”字语义功能分析
sources.summary_en: An article on uses of 以 in the text of 搜神记. It discusses temporal uses and presents 以后 as a fixed temporal construction, but its excerpt does not demonstrate that 以 independently means 'reference point' in the target word.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, sentence-initial 以后 marks the following event as occurring after a discourse reference time or event. The available sentence does not specify how much time passes, and the word itself does not supply an interval.

后 contributes the temporal 'later/after' orientation in the whole word: 以后 refers to a time or period after the present or another stated time. The sources attest constructions such as 自中兴以后 and 自今以后, but they do not establish that 以 independently means 'the reference point' here.

以后 can occur in past narrative, as in the supplied sense, and the cited linguistic study also describes uses with present, future, and habitual reference. That study distinguishes it from 后来, which it describes as past-only, and 然后, which tends to mark successive events.
Older examples establish that 以后 was used in historical texts, but the examples opened here do not prove a historical derivation of the modern word or resolve the separate semantic contribution of 以.

claims.text_en: In the supplied modern examples, 任 precedes an office title and predicates the office the person serves in: 任洛阳北都尉, 任顿丘令. The dictionaries directly list 担任 and 任职 under related undertake/serve senses, while also recording appointment as a separate sense.

Lexicographic sources record related senses for 任, including carrying or bearing, undertaking, duty or responsibility, office, appointment, and serving in a post. These senses make an association between bearing responsibility and holding office conceivable, but the sources opened do not demonstrate that historical development or prove that the target construction derives from the carrying sense.

sources.summary_en: Reports the Shuowen gloss 見不審也 for 佛, interpreted there as not seeing clearly, and says early texts often use 佛 with 仿 in 仿佛, meaning roughly ‘seem/as if.’ It cites Huainanzi and Yang Xiong. This preserves a historical lexicographic analysis; it does not by itself prove a direct derivation of all modern senses.

sources.title: 說文解字「佛」及段玉裁《說文解字注》
sources.summary_en: The Shuowen entry glosses 佛 as 見不審也 and analyzes it as 从人、弗聲. Duan Yucai glosses it 仿佛也 and notes 髴 as an alternate form. This documents an old association between 佛 and indistinct seeing, but Duan's circular gloss does not establish how 佛 contributes to the modern word.

sources.title: 《淮南子·俶真训》原文
sources.summary_en: The text includes 无有仿佛 in a description of primordial, indistinct emptiness. This attests an early occurrence of the word, but the context is not the modern physical-resemblance example and does not alone prove a semantic development.

claims.text_en: For the supplied modern senses, the MOE dictionary groups 仿佛 under 似乎、好像、近似. This supports an overlap between seeming and approximate likeness, but it does not demonstrate two separate modern component meanings. Its entry also does not restrict 近似 to appearance or form.

The historical record gives 佛 a semantic association with unclear or indistinct seeing: Shuowen glosses it 見不審也, and CUHK reports early 仿佛 usage with a ‘seem/as if’ sense. That evidence means 佛 cannot be characterized as only a sound element in every historical account. It does not show that 佛 independently contributes that meaning in present-day 仿佛.

Duan Yucai's note under 仿 analyzes 仿佛 as a 雙聲疊字 expression and gives both ‘similar’ and ‘seeing unclearly’ glosses. This is historical lexicographic interpretation of the expression, not proof that the modern meanings are compositionally derived from the individual characters.

The Huainanzi occurrence 无有仿佛 appears in a passage about indistinct primordial emptiness. It supports early attestation of 仿佛, but that context should not be substituted for the modern resemblance sense or treated as proof of a step-by-step derivation to it.

The sources opened here do not establish whether 佛 remains a productive semantic contributor in modern 仿佛. For current use, the supported account is that 仿佛 functions as a conventional word spanning ‘seem/as if’ and ‘be approximately alike’; a component-by-component explanation of both senses remains unsupported.

sources.title: Ministry of Education 《Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary》: 住
sources.summary_en: The entry defines the verb’s first sense as long-term residence and gives examples meaning “I live in Taipei” and “Where does your family live?” It lists lodging and stopping as separate senses. The long-term qualifier is the dictionary’s wording; the supplied example establishes residence in Zhuo County but does not itself specify duration.

sources.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 住
sources.summary_en: The database analyzes 住 as 从人、主声, gives stopping as its original meaning, and documents later senses including remaining and residing. Its examples for residence include 《世說新語》 and Tang poetry. It does not specify a distinct semantic contribution of 人 to the modern residence sense.

sources.title: 汉语词汇史漫谈 | 汪维辉：古代人如何“居住”
sources.summary_en: In this historical overview, Zhejiang University professor Wang Weihui discusses dated textual examples and argues that 住 developed from standing/staying through lodging to residence, with residence use appearing by the late Han–Three Kingdoms period and becoming dominant by the Eastern Jin. The article notes that some early examples can be read as either stopping or residing. This is the author's historical account, not proof that every step is an established derivation.

sources.title: Continuance Markers of Kaizhou Dialect in Chongqing Municipality
sources.summary_en: The paper concerns a continuative aspect marker in Kaizhou dialect. Its abstract proposes that this marker developed from a Middle Chinese stop/cease sense of 住. That account concerns a dialectal grammatical use; it does not establish the history of the modern residence sense. The earlier dossier's description of the paper as citing Middle Chinese residence and stop/remain examples was not verified on the opened page.

claims.text_en: The target sense is “live; reside.” The Ministry of Education dictionary separately labels a residence sense as long-term residence and gives examples of living in a city and asking where someone lives; the supplied sentence likewise places the person in Zhuo County but does not specify how long they have lived there.

The consulted character analysis describes 住 as 从人、主声: 人 is the semantic component and 主 supplies the sound. This supports a broad human-related component, but does not show that 人 independently contributes the specific meaning “reside” or explain how the character’s parts yield that word sense.

The historical account by Wang Weihui argues that the residence sense developed from earlier standing/staying meanings, through lodging, and reports residence examples by the late Han–Three Kingdoms period and predominant use by the Eastern Jin. Some early examples are explicitly described as ambiguous between staying and residing, so this account supports a proposed lexical development without making every transitional step certain.

The sources differ on the earliest meaning: the CUHK database calls stopping the original meaning, while Wang's account calls standing the original meaning and proposes a stand–stay–lodge–reside path. The Kaizhou dialect study's proposed derivation of an aspect marker from a stop/cease sense concerns a separate grammatical use and does not resolve this disagreement about the residence sense.

claims.text_en: In the supplied sense, 劝 is verbal influence directed at getting another person to act or refrain from acting. The definition and the study’s speech-causation analysis support describing this as an intended influence; the word alone does not state that the person complies.

Older lexicographic evidence glosses 勸 as 勉, and records encouragement or exhortation; the same references also give a use meaning to guide another person verbally. These attestations distinguish the older encouragement sense from the supplied interpersonal sense, but by themselves do not prove the historical derivation between them.

The traditional form 勸 is analyzed as containing 力 with 雚 as the phonetic element. The cited entries do not establish a more precise semantic contribution of 力 to the modern word, so a specific compositional explanation would go beyond the evidence.

A 2023 study reports a shift from an early encouragement meaning toward prominent speech-verb use from the Warring States period onward. The available evidence here supports attributing that account to the study, but does not establish the intervening semantic steps as a proven derivation.

claims.text_en: For the supplied modal use, 可以 functions as a unitary auxiliary meaning that an action is possible or permitted. The sources do not support assigning 以 an independent, useful meaning in this modern use.

A journal abstract proposes a historical path from auxiliary 可 plus prepositional 以 to lexicalized auxiliary 可以 when 以’s object was unexpressed and unrecoverable. This supports lexicalization as a scholarly account, but the abstract does not demonstrate that every older use or every modern modal sense followed that path.

A pre-Qin study analyzes some older 可以 constructions compositionally: 以 is a preposition meaning ‘as’, and its object is placed in the following subject position. A separate review reports an analysis in which early 以 could indicate the preceding subject’s relation to the later action, such as as its instrument or means. These historical analyses show that 以 could contribute in older constructions; they do not establish a separate contribution in the modern modal.

In the supplied sentence, 可以依靠 is modal: the three people had no official position they could rely on. The example supports the modern auxiliary reading, but does not distinguish a semantic contribution by 以 from the meaning of 可以 as a whole.

sources.summary_en: The opened journal page gives the abstract of Wang Jinhui’s article. It describes a proposed grammaticalization path from comitative verb to comitative preposition to coordinate conjunction, and explicitly says the comitative prepositions 共、和、同、跟 that emerged after the Medieval period followed that path. claims.text_en: In the supplied coordination sense, 和 connects coordinate items such as nouns or pronouns. In a phrase such as 我和你, it marks the coordination relation between 我 and 你; it does not specify an action they perform. The sources also document 和 between the final two items in lists of three or more.

In the supplied “with” sense, 和 introduces a person who participates with the subject or serves as the counterpart in an interaction. In 和有志的人交朋友, the phrase identifies the person with whom the subject is willing to make friends; 和 is not linking two noun phrases as coordinated items.

The conjunction and preposition uses are grammatically distinguishable: conjunction 和 links elements on both sides, while prepositional 和 introduces a participant or counterpart associated with the following action. 我和你一起做大事 permits a coordination reading (“you and I”) and a comitative reading (“I, together with you”); 一起 is compatible with the latter but does not by itself rule out the former.

A scholarly article’s abstract proposes the development path comitative verb → comitative preposition → coordinate conjunction and explicitly includes 和 among the comitative prepositions said to have followed that path after the Medieval period. This is the author’s historical analysis; the opened abstract alone does not expose its dated examples or establish the detailed chronology independently.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 国家 is the conventional word for a country or nation: a political community understood as a whole. One historical account explains its parts through the fiefs of lords and senior officials: 国 referred to a lord’s domain, while 家 could refer to a senior official’s estate or governed domain. Another scholarly account describes 家’s family living-space sense taking on a political sense and 国 and 家 blending into the compound; these accounts do not establish one certain path for every early use.

claims.text_en: In ancient political usage, 家 could refer to the stipend estate or governed domain of a senior official, rather than simply a household. The Han Dian Guoyu entry distinguishes that 家 from a lord’s 国; the specialist terminology entry similarly describes 家 as a dafu’s fief.

One specialist terminology account presents 国家 as a combined term for those two kinds of fief and describes a later extension to a country’s whole territory and then to a modern political entity. This supports a historical political contribution for 家, but is that source’s account of development rather than proof that every early use followed this path.

A scholarly article abstract gives a related but distinct account: 家’s family living-space sense became political space under Zhou institutions, and 国 and 家 blended into 国家 during the Warring States period. The current sense “country; nation” is also supported by Han Dian’s definition of 国家 as a political group and its translations.

sources.title: On Structural Particles in Sinitic Languages: Typology and Diachrony
sources.summary_en: Giorgio Francesco Arcodia’s survey describes 地 as the Standard Mandarin marker connecting adverbial modifiers to verbs. It reports Medieval Chinese 地 with adverbs and various patterns of reduplicated state adjectives, and reviews competing historical analyses. sources.summary_en: The Taiwan Ministry of Education dictionary lists 地 pronounced de as a structural particle used after adverbs, with examples such as 慢慢地吃 and 好好地玩. It separately lists dì pronunciations and uses, including noun meanings.

claims.text_en: In 长长地叹气, 长长 provides the descriptive content and modifies 叹气; 地 marks the adverbial relation between modifier and verb. 地 itself does not mean ‘long’ or specify the sound or manner of the sigh. The dictionary and survey support this modifier-plus-地 construction; the supplied sentence establishes its use here.

The target is adverbial 地, distinct in grammatical function from 地 meaning a place or ground, nominal-modifying 的, and complement-marking 得. Lin distinguishes the three corresponding Late Medieval construction types; Arcodia notes that the three Standard Mandarin particles are now homophonous but written with different characters.

Arcodia reports that Medieval Chinese 地 occurred with adverbs and various patterns of reduplicated state adjectives, rather than initially with non-reduplicated adjectives. The survey describes the Standard Mandarin marker as becoming available with a broader range of adjectives. These reported distributions do not, on their own, prove a direct derivation into the modern construction.

Arcodia reviews a proposal deriving adverbial 地 from the locative noun 地 ‘place’ through reanalysis, and a different proposal that 地 took over a manner-marking role associated with older suffixes on state adjectives. The survey favors an adjectival-suffix source construction for 地-type markers, but this remains a proposed historical account, not a demonstrated derivation of the modern Standard Mandarin particle.

claims.text_en: For the supplied modern sense, the best-supported compositional reading is that 声 contributes the conventional idea of renown, reputation, or prestige, rather than literal audible sound. 势 contributes force, power, or an imposing condition or presence: these are listed senses of 势, and the dictionary entry for 气势 includes strength, authority, bearing, and style. Reading 声势 as prestige or renown together with force or imposing presence is a supported compositional interpretation, not a demonstrated historical derivation.

声势 is also attested in older senses for mutual military support and for power or status; the dictionary cites historical texts for these uses. Those attestations establish older uses, but the sources opened do not show that either sense developed into the modern sense of 声威和气势.

“Momentum” appears as an English rendering in the 声势 dictionary entry, including for its separate military-support sense. The Chinese definitions opened do not establish momentum as an independent contribution of 声 or as a distinct core component of the supplied modern sense; it may be a context-sensitive translation.

sources.title: 关于“就”字的释义
sources.summary_en: This page reproduces dictionary-style entries that distinguish adverbial 就 for an event occurring early or ending early from 就 for an event occurring within a short time and for sequential events. Its example 他十五岁就参加革命了 supports the early-time classification. The page is hosted by a university office, rather than being the dictionary itself.

sources.title: 从“就”看词义的形成、分项和识别
sources.summary_en: Zuo Simin’s article describes the early-occurrence reading and distinguishes it from the imminent/short-time and sequential readings. It argues that early occurrence can be a pragmatic implication of a short-time meaning in a suitable temporal and aspectual context; this is the author’s analysis, not an uncontested derivation. It also records older verbal senses such as moving toward, returning, or taking up a post, but does not document their development into the modern early-time use.

sources.title: 你了解“就”的用法吗？ / Consejos prácticos para el uso correcto del adverbio jiù
sources.summary_en: An Instituto Confucio language article distinguishes early occurrence, commonly preceded by a time expression, from occurrence within a short time and from sequential events. Its examples include 从小 and other time expressions before 就. It supports the target construction pattern, though its example 从小我们就是好朋友 also contains 是 and is not identical to the supplied sentence.

claims.text_en: In 刘备家里很穷，从小就有大志, 从小 sets the temporal frame as childhood onward. 就 marks the state 有大志 as true from that early point; the sentence does not specify a more exact age or date. This is the early-occurrence use, not the imminent-use meaning. The dictionary-style entry classifies this early reading separately and illustrates it with 他十五岁就参加革命了; the specialist article describes temporal material before 就 as a diagnostic context for the early reading.

The supplied sense is distinct from 就 meaning that something will happen within a short time, as in 我就来, and from 就 linking successive events. The ECNU article proposes that the early reading may be inferred pragmatically from a more general short-time meaning in an appropriate context. sources.title: A Diachronic Investigation on the Lexical Formation and Evolution of the Chinese Adverb “Yijing (已经)”
sources.summary_en: The authors propose a historical account in which jing develops grammatical functions in yi+jing constructions and the whole yijing structure lexicalizes. They discuss competing dating proposals and acknowledge that their Tang corpus does not cover all relevant material. This is the authors’ proposed analysis, not proof that modern 经 has a separable meaning in 已经.

sources.title: A Semantic Study on the Adverb ‘YIJING’
sources.summary_en: Lee analyzes 已经 in terms of anteriority relative to a reference time and argues that pragmatic effects such as counter-expectation or confirmation depend on context. The paper offers a particular semantic analysis, not a component-by-component account.

sources.title: Feature Representations and Logical Compatibility between Temporal Adverbs and Aspects
sources.summary_en: This corpus-based study classifies 已经 as reference-time-related: it places a situation before a specific time, another event or situation, or speech time. It gives examples with both past and future reference times.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 已经 marks a situation as anterior to a contextually relevant time. That time can be a past or future specific time, another event or situation, or speech time; it need not be the moment of speaking. This fits the examples in which a battle has ended or a person has reached a particular age by the time under discussion.

A supported learner explanation treats 已经 as a conventional adverb meaning ‘already’ or ‘by the relevant time, the situation had occurred or become true.’ The dictionary defines the whole word, and the modern semantic studies describe the word as an adverb. The sources reviewed do not establish a distinct, learner-useful present-day meaning contributed independently by 经 here. That is a limit of the evidence reviewed, not proof that no such analysis exists.

One diachronic study proposes that older 经 in yi+jing constructions could occur with material interpreted as an experienced object, and that later contexts allowed reanalysis with verb phrases. In the authors’ account, jing with activity predicates developed a manner use glossed ‘through’, while other predicate contexts developed past or perfect functions; reanalysis and lexicalization then produced adverbial 已经. These are proposed stages in that study’s historical account, not evidence that modern 经 independently means ‘through’ or ‘experience’ in the supplied sense.

The diachronic study reports differing proposals for when 已经 formed as a word or adverb: one account places adverb formation by the Song, another argues for word formation in the Liang, and later proposals dispute Tang dating or place formation in the Later Tang and Five Dynasties. The study itself proposes early lexicalized use in the seventh century and completion by the Song, while noting that its Tang corpus is incomplete. The historical derivation and chronology therefore remain unsettled in the sources reviewed.

Lee’s semantic study treats anteriority as the core meaning of 已经 and argues that effects such as counter-expectation or confirmation arise in context. This supports leaving those effects out of a shared definition unless a particular occurrence calls for them.

claims.text_en: 張角 is attested as a person's name for the Eastern Han figure associated with the Yellow Turban movement. sources.title: “当”的演变过程
sources.summary_en: The article discusses 当 before temporal expressions in examples such as 当今 and 当是时, analyzing it there as ‘at/during’ and as a preposition developed from a verb use. It does not establish that the modern word 当时 derives from that construction.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 当时 refers to a contextually identified time, commonly rendered ‘at that time’ or ‘then.’ The example uses it for the period when the epidemic was widespread. The dictionaries support this broad temporal reading; ‘then’ is a contextual paraphrase rather than evidence for a separate component meaning.

时 supplies the time reference in the compound. The role of 当 in the modern word is less certain: the temporal use of 当 before a time expression is attested in constructions such as 当是时, but that parallel does not demonstrate the historical formation or precise contribution of 当时 as a lexical item.

The dictionaries also record an ‘immediately; at once’ use, but disagree about its pronunciation: the MOE dictionary places it under dāngshí, while 漢語網 assigns it to dàngshí. 漢語網 additionally lists historical uses such as ‘people of the time,’ ‘the reigning emperor,’ ‘in one’s prime,’ and ‘timely’; these are distinct from the supplied ordinary temporal sense.

claims.text_en: In the supplied example, 悬念 concerns the unresolved question of whether Dong Zhuo survives: the story leaves his fate open and invites expectation about the outcome. This is the narrative sense of audience anticipation, not the personal sense of being concerned about someone.

As a cautious synchronic reading of the word’s parts, 悬 can evoke a hanging or unresolved state, while 念 contributes the sense of thinking about, keeping in mind, or mental attention. Together these meanings fit expectation focused on an unsettled plot or fate. The opened sources do not establish this as the proven historical derivation of the narrative sense.

悬念 also has a distinct personal-concern sense. The Ministry dictionary records it with a Tang attestation; the narrative sense is separately attested in a 1982 quotation cited by 漢典. These attestations document the senses, but do not establish when the narrative sense arose or how it developed from the personal-concern sense.

A linguistic study's brief, schematic historical account reports that 找 entered use during the Ming period and displaced 寻 as the central search-field lexeme by mid-Qing. This account explains a possible history of that separate sense, not the origin of the seeking sense itself.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 抵抗 means resisting or opposing. It can describe military opposition, as in the supplied example, but the dictionary material also applies it to nonmilitary adverse conditions such as drought and flooding; an armed opponent is therefore not required by the general sense.

The dictionary entries document overlapping resistance-related verbal senses for both parts: 抵 can mean to block or resist, and 抗 can mean to ward off or resist. This supports an interpretation of the compound as combining closely related contributions. That compositional reading is an inference from the definitions, not evidence of a specific historical formation process.

The character entries cite older resistance-related uses: 抵 is illustrated with a 水滸傳 passage, while 抗 is illustrated with passages from 列子 and Han Yu. These citations attest relevant older senses of the components; they do not by themselves establish when or how the modern compound 抵抗 developed.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 故事 means a story or narrated account. It is distinct from the older dictionary sense 'precedent; customary rule.' The sources also describe older uses such as former affairs, historical events, and allusions, which should not replace the supplied narrative sense.

施爱东’s account supports a broad historical shift in use: older canonical examples mostly concern precedents, old systems, former work, or historical events; Ming-Qing vernacular examples use 故事 for matter that is told or heard, including material that may be fictional. This supports development of a narrative use, but does not establish a single direct semantic path for every modern use.

The article reports that late-Qing periodicals selected 故事 to translate English Story and repeatedly used it in narrative titles, strengthening its public association with a narrative genre. The same article says literary narrative use was already present by the late Ming, so the translation activity is not evidence that all narrative uses originated from English Story.

A limited component-level observation is possible: 故 can mean 'former' or 'old' in older usages, and 事 can refer to an affair or event; together these fit some older senses of 故事 such as 'former affairs' or 'precedent.' The 2024 article proposes a broader shared 'affair' basis, but isolated component senses and older compound uses do not prove that the current narrative meaning is compositionally derived from them. The modern sense’s precise derivation remains unresolved.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 故意 means acting with intent or purpose. The Ministry of Education dictionary glosses it as 存心的、有意的; the supplied example supports 'intentionally retreated' without specifying the reason or motive for the retreat.

There is some synchronic support for a transparent reading of 故意: the Ministry of Education lists 有意、存心 as a sense of 故, while its entry for 意 includes thought, idea, and wish. These component entries make an intentional interpretation plausible, but they do not assign a precise separate contribution to each part. In particular, the entry for 意 does not itself define it as 'intention' here.

故意 is established as a dictionary word with the target meaning, and its components have related contemporary meanings. It is reasonable to describe it as semantically transparent to some extent, but the consulted sources do not prove that the modern compound was originally formed by composition, nor that 故 historically modified 意 in this word.

史有為 reports Yuan and Ming examples of adverbial 故意. The author proposes that predicate uses such as 是故意的 developed from the adverbial use by making an implicit 'do that way' part explicit, while presenting that account as dependent on the reported chronology. This proposal concerns later grammatical use; it does not establish how the compound first acquired its intentional sense.

The modern intentional sense should be kept distinct from the separately listed literary sense 'old friends' affection' and the legal sense. Their presence under the same spelling does not demonstrate that either is historically derived from, or gave rise to, the modern adverbial sense.

claims.text_en: In the supplied sense, 敵人 means a person who has enmity toward and opposes one’s side. The dictionary example shows that opposing positions can make former friends 敵人; the word is not restricted to a military enemy.

The word has a transparent component reading: 敵 contributes ‘enemy/opponent’ and 人 contributes ‘person.’ This is a supported word-part analysis; the dictionaries define 敵人 as a whole and do not present this segmentation as a historical derivation.

An older cited use of 敵人 occurs in Wenxin Diaolong in a discussion of argumentation, where an adversary might exploit a weakness. Han Dian also cites the compound from Guanzi. These attestations support an adversarial use of the compound, but do not show the precise historical path by which it formed or developed.

Shuowen glosses 敵 with 仇, and Duan Yucai’s note discusses related adversarial and contending senses. This contextualizes 敵 but does not prove that those older senses directly produced the modern compound’s meaning.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 救 means to aid and help someone out of difficulty or danger. The dictionary’s definition does not specify a method or type of danger, so the broad gloss “save; rescue” fits. The example gives no further detail about what or whom is being rescued.

The component analysis does not transparently encode the modern aid/rescue meaning: the cited analyses assign 求 a phonetic role, while the Shuowen entry gives 攴 as the other component. sources.summary_en: The page previews a 2008 article in 理论语言学研究 and reproduces its abstract and part of its discussion. The author proposes that the adverb developed through frequent co-occurrence of the past-time adverb 曾 and the verb 经 ‘undergo/experience’, followed by lexicalization and reanalysis. sources.title: 牛春燕，基于HSK语料库的定时时间副词“曾经”习得研究
sources.summary_en: This 2023 study treats target modern 曾经 as a time adverb indicating that a behavior or situation existed or occurred before speaking, and describes it as modifying verbs or adjectives. It does not analyze a distinct modern contribution from 经 or establish the word’s historical derivation.

claims.text_en: For the target present-day adverb, 曾经 as a whole marks a behavior or situation as having occurred or existed previously. The cited dictionary and modern usage study describe the word at the whole-word level; neither supports assigning 经 an independent ‘experience’ meaning in each modern use.

The historical 曾 + 经 account is an explicit proposal by 丁健: the author treats 曾 as an already existing past-time adverb and 经 as a verb meaning ‘undergo/experience’, and proposes that frequent co-occurrence led to lexicalization and reanalysis. This gives a possible historical explanation for the form, but does not show that 经 contributes that lexical meaning independently in the modern adverb.

The article preview reports examples of the sequence 曾经 in Eastern Han texts but also presents them as co-occurrences of the two elements. An early sequence alone therefore does not establish that the modern adverb already existed then. The author’s proposed chronology—beginnings in Tang, formation in mid-Qing, maturity from late Qing to the early Republic—is an analysis reported by this one previewed article, not independently confirmed here.

claims.text_en: For the supplied aspiration sense, 有志 means having aspirations or ambitions. sources.summary_en: Defines the target sense as 才能、能力 and cites an older skill/ability use in Tang text. It also lists senses translated as gist/essentials, principal/important, and source/root, with quotations. The page's separate character glosses include 本 meanings such as source and original, and a 领 meaning related to a subject's outline; it does not connect these glosses to the target sense.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense “ability; skill,” the consulted dictionary entries define 本领 as a whole: 本事、能力 or 才学、技能. They do not assign a distinct contribution to 本 or 领 in that sense, so a word-level explanation is supported.

The sources record other meanings of 本领, including “originally; fundamentally,” “gist; essentials,” “principal; important,” and “source; root.” The Tang quotation cited by 汉语国学 attests a skill-related use, but the consulted sources do not show that any of the other senses—or a separate meaning of 本 or 领—historically produced the modern ability/skill sense.

汉语国学 lists character-level meanings for 本 and 领 separately, including meanings that might look compositional. Its entry does not say those character meanings explain 本领 as “ability; skill”; treating them as the word's components would go beyond the evidence in that source.

claims.text_en: For the supplied historical military-title sense, the pronunciation is xiào wèi: the Ministry dictionary and Han Dian’s main compound entry both give this reading. Han Dian’s separate 國語辭典 section gives jiào wèi, a discrepancy within that page.

A useful learner-oriented breakdown is 校 | 尉. In the xiào reading, 校 has an attested ancient military-unit sense, and Han Dian specifically glosses 校尉 there as an officer leading such a unit. 尉 wèi is attested as an ancient official title associated with military affairs. These senses support the component explanation, but do not by themselves prove the compound’s historical derivation.
The historical title should not be equated with a modern military rank. The dictionaries describe an older official title and its historical status; they provide no exact modern rank mapping.

claims.text_en: In this entry, 桓帝 is a historical ruler designation, not the ruler’s personal name. The *Hou Hanshu* gives the formal title as 孝桓皇帝 and states that his personal name (諱) was 志. The entry’s shorter form 桓帝 corresponds to this ruler in the Eastern Han annals.

The examples identify the Eastern Han Emperor Huan: the *Hou Hanshu* records his death, then says Dou Wu and Chen Fan jointly administered the court after the emperor’s death; the following emperor’s annals identify that ruler as 孝桓皇帝 and describe the succession that brought in Emperor Ling.

In this title, 桓 is the posthumous-name element: the *Hou Hanshu* explicitly cites the *Shi fa* saying 克敵服遠曰桓. 帝 identifies the ruler as an emperor. This supports the title’s components; it does not by itself explain the broader historical practice of assigning posthumous titles.

sources.title: 多义词“气”的“愤怒义”源流探析
sources.summary_en: This 2023 article proposes a history in which 气 develops from cloud vapor and bodily or physiological qi toward anger-related uses, then appears as a standalone verb in Yuan-period vernacular texts. Its explanation involving bodily conceptualization, omitted material, and vernacular usage is the authors’ proposal; the attestations alone do not establish every causal step.

claims.text_en: In the supplied phrase 张飞又气又不满, 气 describes Zhang Fei as angry or feeling anger. The wording does not specify the cause or a narrower type of anger. Han Dian and 国台对照活用辞典 both list an intransitive anger sense for 气.

The anger-state use is distinct from transitive 气 meaning ‘make someone angry’: both dictionaries list the transitive use separately. In the supplied phrase, Zhang Fei is the person experiencing the anger.

A 2023 article proposes that anger-related uses developed against an older background of bodily meanings and associations between qi and anger. It points to older expressions such as 气急 and bodily-qi references alongside anger, and argues that standalone verbal 气 is attested in Yuan drama, with later examples in novels. These are the article’s historical analysis and attestations; they do not by themselves prove the proposed causal path from the older bodily senses to the modern anger verb.
For the target verbal sense, 气 is not compositionally glossed as ‘breath’ or ‘vital energy.’ The older bodily-qi material is relevant only as background to the article’s proposed history.

claims.text_en: For the target verbal sense, 活 means to live or remain alive (生存). The Ministry of Education’s revised dictionary cites classical examples from the Book of Odes and a poem by Du Fu for this sense.

The revised dictionary distinguishes the target intransitive sense 生存 from an adjectival use meaning 有生命的 and a separate verbal sense meaning 救助. The Ministry of Education’s concise dictionary also distinguishes 生存 from 使生存, supporting the distinction between living and causing someone or something to live.

Duan Yucai’s commentary reports an older gloss related to flowing water and explicitly calls the use meaning ‘not dead’ an extension, citing the Odes and Mencius. This documents Duan’s proposed explanation; the page does not provide a dated chain establishing how that extension developed into the ordinary modern verb sense.

In 董卓能不能活下来, the question is whether Dong Zhuo will remain alive. The sentence does not specify how he might do so. The dictionary supports the 活 survival sense, but the consulted sources do not establish a more precise contribution for 来 in this occurrence.

The supplied reading Zhuōxiàn is not directly attested by the opened dictionary entry for 涿县. The character dictionary lists zhuō as an alternate reading, whereas the specific entry 涿郡 is read zhuó jùn. sources.summary_en: Li Daoyuan reports earlier statements that 涿郡 lay south of 涿水, then proposes that 涿 was named from the water and that the commandery and county inherited that name. He qualifies this as possibly close but not secure, so the text supports a reported hypothesis rather than a settled derivation.

sources.title: 郡 — Ministry of Education Revised Mandarin Dictionary
sources.summary_en: Defines 郡 as the name of an ancient Chinese local administrative region and describes its changing relation to 县 across periods. This supports the administrative contribution of 郡 in 涿郡.

claims.text_en: 郡 contributes the administrative classification “commandery”: the dictionary defines it as an ancient local administrative region, and CHGIS classifies this 涿郡 as a commandery with 涿县 as its seat. “Zhuo Commandery” is therefore supported as a rendering of the name.
涿 is the inherited proper-name element in 涿郡, also found in the seat name 涿县. The gazetteer and character dictionary document these names but do not by themselves explain the origin of 涿.

Historical sources offer a water-name explanation, with differing levels of certainty. 水经注 proposes that 涿郡 and 涿县 took 涿 from 涿水, but explicitly qualifies the proposal as uncertain. 太平寰宇记 states more directly that the Han commandery was named after 涿水. These attest a historical explanation; they do not independently establish the derivation.

The Shuowen Jiezi tradition glosses 涿 as flowing or dripping downward and analyzes it as 从水，豖声. The sources opened do not connect that lexical gloss to the historical place-name, so it should not be used as an explanation of 涿郡.

sources.summary_en: The historical study says Han emperors’ posthumous names followed a stable 孝 + identifying epithet structure and that later usage commonly used the identifying epithet as the abbreviated posthumous name. sources.title: Emperor Huan and Emperor Ling: being the chronicle of the Later Han Dynasty for the years 157 to 189 AD as recorded in chapters 54 to 59 of the Zizhi tongjian of Sima Guang
sources.summary_en: The Australian National University repository identifies this as Rafe de Crespigny’s 1989 translated and annotated work, and its title uses the conventional English form “Emperor Ling.” The catalogue record confirms the translation’s title and publication details; it does not itself explain the Chinese naming convention.

claims.text_en: For Liu Hong, 靈 is part of his posthumous name, not a temple name: the Hou Hanshu identifies him as 孝靈皇帝 and cites the posthumous-name rule 亂而不損曰靈; a historical listing separately records no temple name and the posthumous name 孝靈皇帝.

In this designation, 靈 is the identifying posthumous epithet. 帝 marks the emperor designation, reflected in the established English rendering “Emperor Ling.” The cited historical study explains the shortened Chinese form: Han imperial posthumous names used 孝 plus an identifying epithet, and later usage commonly abbreviated them by the epithet, yielding forms such as 靈帝 from 孝靈皇帝.

The full posthumous name includes 孝, but the conventional shortened designation used here is 靈帝. The sources support that abbreviation as part of the broader Han naming practice; “Emperor Ling” is attested as the English conventional form in the ANU scholarly translation’s title.

These are reported older uses, not evidence by themselves that modern person-target 相信 descended from reciprocal 相信. The directly opened 《谷梁传》 page could not be retrieved for independent verification.

信 is the clearest semantic anchor for the modern belief/trust meaning. This is a component-level inference from dictionary definitions and the reported historical uses, not an explicit morphological analysis establishing how the modern compound formed.

Modern 相信 can take either a person or a proposition as its object, and the specialist comparison says it generally lacks the reciprocal pattern found in 相互信任. Thus the supplied person-target sense does not imply mutual or reciprocal belief.

In the Zhuangzi passage cited by the historical study, 知道 occurs in a discussion of thinking and knowing 道, alongside 安道 and 得道. The surrounding text and commentary make this a specifically philosophical use; here 道 functions as the thing known, rather than providing evidence that 道 means “reason” or “rule” in every use of 知道.

The 2024 study proposes a historical development from older compositional uses involving 道理, 道义, or 规律 to a broader sense of knowing things generally. This is the author's historical analysis. The opened Zhuangzi passage supports an older “know 道” context, but does not by itself verify the proposed broader chain of development or prove that it is the source of the modern word.

The available sources do not establish a distinct semantic contribution by 道 in the supplied modern general sense. The defensible modern explanation is the word-level meaning “know; be aware of”; the older “know 道” use is a possible historical connection, not a proven derivation.

A reasonable structural parse is 程 as the surname and 远志 as the given name. The dictionary attests 远志 as ‘far-reaching aspiration’ in older texts, so that is a possible lexical reading of the given name; the sources do not show that the novelist intended this meaning for the character.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 竟然 is used as a whole adverb to mark an event or result as unexpected or contrary to expectation. The dictionary defines the word as unexpectedly; the 2010 study likewise describes the 竟然 class as signaling an outcome contrary to expectation and modifying its clause predicate.

A defensible grammatical description is that 然 belongs to the suffix-like 然 element found in X然 adverbs: Shao explicitly classifies 然 this way while treating 竟然 as an adverb. This does not establish a distinct present-day meaning for 然 within 竟然; the sources describe the unexpectedness at the whole-word level.

Shao proposes a general X然 development in which forms used to describe a state as predicates came to precede and modify other predicates, with 然’s meaning becoming more attenuated. This is a proposed class-level account, not proof that the modern 竟然 sense derives from a particular older meaning of either component.

The Osaka dissertation cautions that X然 adverb meanings and functions can be related to both X and 然 and to the construction’s sentence position, but its case study is 确然. It therefore cannot independently establish what 然 contributes specifically in 竟然.

This attests an older 结为 phrase and a complement-oriented analysis on that page; it does not prove that the modern construction descends continuously from that example or settle the syntax of modern 结为.

sources.title: 結拜兄弟 - 教育百科 | 教育雲線上字典
sources.summary_en: The entry, drawing on Taiwan’s Ministry of Education dictionary, defines sworn brothers as brothers joined through a close relationship; a Hakka dictionary entry on the page says they are non-blood-related brothers formed through closeness or a common goal. This supports the relationship/status sense of 结为兄弟 without implying biological kinship.

claims.text_en: In the target use, 结 contributes joining or forming a bond: dictionaries give the relational sense and examples such as 结为夫妇, while 汉典 also lists 聚、合 and compounds including 结盟 and 结交. This contribution is supported; it does not mean that every sense of 结 is relevant here.

为 is read wéi and contributes a resulting ‘become’ sense: the dictionary explicitly lists 变成 under wéi. In 三人结为兄弟, 兄弟 names the resulting relationship/status, so a cautious paraphrase is ‘the three become/form a brother-like relationship.’ The exact syntactic label for 为 in modern 结为 is not established by the opened dictionary entry.

The target sense is relationship- or status-forming, not an unrestricted ‘become any state.’ Dictionary examples include 结为夫妇, and the education-dictionary entry describes 结拜兄弟 as a non-biological relationship. The example 三人结为兄弟 supports a relationship reading but does not by itself specify a ritual, motive, or biological identity.

A grammar reference cites the Shiji wording 乃结为亲友 in a complement-pattern section. This is evidence that a 结为 phrase with a relationship/status expression is attested in an older text and has been analyzed there in a complement framework. It does not prove a direct historical derivation or uninterrupted continuity to the modern construction.

Shuowen gives 結 the gloss 締也, and the cited character analysis is 糸 plus 吉 as phonetic. This is consistent with the older tying/binding sense of 结, but an older gloss alone does not establish that the modern relationship-forming construction 结为 developed directly from it.

sources.title: Sworn Brothers: A Study in Chinese Ritual Kinship
sources.summary_en: Jordan’s study describes jiébài xiōngdì as a form of fictive kinship used for close friendships and for economic or political purposes. Its account says the ideal ritual involved an oath, but reports that formal elements could be absent and that groups selected different practices and obligations.

sources.summary_en: Reproduces Taiwan’s Ministry of Education revised dictionary definition of 結拜兄弟 as brothers who have formed sworn kinship because of close affection. This supports the conventional social-kinship reading of the related expression.

sources.title: 桃园三结义原文及翻译、朗读_《三国演义》文言文_古文岛
sources.summary_en: Presents the Peach Garden episode as text from the Ming novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms. The passage uses 既结为兄弟 and follows it with a pledge of joint action; the page identifies the passage as literary text, not historical documentation.

claims.text_en: In the supplied construction, 结为 contributes forming or entering a resulting status, and 兄弟 names that status. This is a constructional reading of the phrase, supported by the literary passage’s 既结为兄弟 followed by a description of the resulting bond; the sources do not provide a dedicated grammatical analysis of 结为.

The phrase can be used for brothers by an adopted social bond rather than biological kin. This is supported by dictionary entries for 結拜兄弟 and 結拜, though those related entries do not prove that every occurrence of 结为兄弟 has that interpretation.
Strong affection or a shared purpose are motivations given for the related practice of 結拜. They are not specified by the supplied example 三人结为兄弟 and should not be added to its general gloss.

The Peach Garden passage uses 既结为兄弟 in a context that includes ritual and an oath. As the opened page identifies it as an episode from Romance of the Three Kingdoms, it attests literary use and does not establish that the historical figures performed that ceremony.

The phrase does not by itself establish that every instance involves a formal oath, ritual, or fixed set of obligations. Jordan describes an ideal ritual but also reports that formal elements could be missing and practices varied among groups.

sources.summary_en: Lists the target meaning and several distinct uses, including binding, restraint, packing, dressing, and conclusion. sources.title: 贺国伟，《“结束”曾为装束语》，新浪新闻转载《新民晚报》
sources.summary_en: Proposes that the modern completion sense arose from dressing: tying the garment and belt allegedly marked the final steps of getting dressed, and the sense then broadened to completion generally. The article supplies examples but no scholarly demonstration establishing that semantic path.

claims.text_en: In the supplied sense, 結束 means that something reaches its close or is completed. Both Ministry of Education dictionaries directly support this meaning.

結 independently has a recorded sense ‘end; bring to a close’ (終了、收束), alongside senses involving linking and joining. This makes a closing association for 結 in 結束 plausible, but the character entry alone does not prove the compound’s internal composition.

束 is independently recorded as ‘tie/bind’ and ‘arrange/pack’; the opened Ministry of Education character entry does not give it a standalone ‘end’ sense. These meanings do not establish a distinct 束 contribution to the modern completion sense.

《后汉书》 attests 結束 in a description of clothing made of horizontal strips that are joined. This supports an older clothing-related use in context, but does not establish that the modern sense developed from it.

A newspaper essay proposes that a dressing sense broadened into ‘completion’ because tying and belting were final steps in dressing. The opened evidence does not demonstrate this proposed transition; the attestations of clothing-related uses and modern completion are not by themselves proof of derivation.

sources.title: 解析汉字历史及汉字文化
sources.summary_en: A review of a character-source dictionary reports Cao Xianzhuo's proposed analysis: 朵's earlier sense was protruding or extending, connecting ears to parts projecting sideways from the head. It also reports older glosses about hanging tree growths. This is a reported character-level proposal, not proof that the modern word 耳朵 arose by that derivation.

sources.title: 漢語多功能字庫：朵
sources.summary_en: Gives the Shuowen gloss of 朵 as hanging tree growths and records later accounts concerning flowers, flower classifiers, and other uses. Its presented historical materials do not establish a derivation of the modern compound 耳朵.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 耳朵 means an ear. The Ministry of Education dictionary labels it the colloquial term for the ear; the example about unusually long ears does not narrow the referent to the earlobe or another specific part.

There is a published character-level proposal connecting 朵's older glosses about hanging growths with a broader idea of protruding or extending, and applying that idea to ears projecting from the sides of the head. This makes a shape or position association plausible as an explanation of the character's use, but the source reports an interpretation; it does not demonstrate that present-day speakers assign 朵 a distinct compositional meaning in 耳朵 or establish that interpretation as the word's historical derivation.

The revised Ministry dictionary records a whole-word extension of 耳朵 for something shaped or positioned like an ear and gives a Shuihu Zhuan example about a part of a shoe. This supports an established extended use of the word, but does not show that 朵 alone supplies the shape meaning.

The opened dictionaries support teaching 耳朵 as the conventional word for ‘ear,’ with 耳 identifying the referent. They do not settle whether 朵 retains a distinct shape or position contribution for modern Mandarin speakers, nor whether a historical contribution weakened over time. The available opened evidence does not establish 朵 as a productive suffix in this word.

sources.title: Emergence and Formation of the Modern Chinese Anaphor ZIJI
sources.summary_en: Edith Aldridge analyzes the history of 自己 as a compound of the Late Archaic anaphors 自 and 己. The paper argues that 自 was initially locally bound, while 己 could be locally or long-distance bound; 自 was later reanalyzed as allowing long-distance binding before 自己 formed. It presents fourth-century examples of 自己 as a possessor and object, and proposes a prosodic difference between 自己 and monosyllabic 己. These are analyses of grammatical history and distribution; they do not establish a distinct modern semantic contribution for each character.

sources.title: 漢語反身代詞“自己”的長距離約束用法及其早期用例 (Long-distance Binding of Chinese Reflexive ‘ziji’(自己): A Diachronic Perspective)
sources.summary_en: The accessible abstract reports that the author finds long-distance binding uses of 自己 in Ming literature, whereas earlier accounts had placed their attestation in the Qing. The article itself was marked unavailable on the opened page, so its evidence and definitions could not be checked.

claims.text_en: In the supplied predicate examples, 自己 refers back to the person identified in the sentence or context: 那人 in the first example and 刘备 in the third. The Ministry of Education dictionary glosses the word as 本身, and Aldridge treats modern 自己 as an anaphor that can be locally or long-distance bound. The antecedent comes from the sentence and context, not from a different English pronoun inherent in 自己.

In 自己的想法, 自己 identifies the person to whom the thoughts relate; the example does not require a narrower claim about legal ownership. 的 follows 自己 and marks the phrase as a modifier of 想法. The dictionary's example 自己心中 also shows 自己 in a self-related nominal expression.

Aldridge proposes a grammatical history in which 自 and 己 were similar reflexive elements by the time 自己 formed: 自 had shifted from requiring a local antecedent to allowing long-distance binding, while 己 already allowed both. This supports a historical account of the compound's binding behavior, but does not show that modern 自 and 己 each contribute a separate, recoverable semantic feature such as “self” versus “own.”

Aldridge cites fourth-century examples of 自己 as a possessor in 自己衣鉢 and as an object in 供給自己, and reports prosodic distribution differences between disyllabic 自己 and monosyllabic 己. These attestations support the paper's account of the compound's early grammatical distribution; they do not by themselves prove how the modern possessive use developed semantically.

There is an unresolved dating discrepancy: Aldridge presents a fourth-century long-distance-bound 自己 example, while Kang's accessible 2018 abstract says the long-distance use previously thought to begin in the Qing is attested in Ming literature. Because Kang's full article was unavailable and the two accounts may classify or analyze the constructions differently, the source pages do not settle the discrepancy.

sources.title: 贿 huì - 汉典
sources.summary_en: Records 贿 as property or valuables, as giving property, and as using property to buy someone off. Its examples support a material-payment contribution without specifying the payment's form or kind.

claims.text_en: In the supplied bribery sense, 行 contributes the verbal idea of doing or carrying out an act: the character entry lists xíng as “do/engage in” and “carry out.” The entry separately lists “circulate” as an older 行贿 use; that is not the supplied sense.

贿 contributes the idea of property or valuables used as a bribe. The character entry also records giving property and using it to buy someone off. The cited entries do not specify what form the payment takes in the supplied sense.

汉典 distinguishes an older 行贿 sense, “circulate property,” from the bribery sense and cites attestations for both. These entries do not establish that the bribery sense developed from the older one; the Tang citation is presented as an attestation, not a derivation.
